standard_prerequisites: A Dedekind infinite set: a set admitting an injection whose range is a proper subset of its domain; a set is Dedekind infinite when such an injection exists.
The natural numbers of the iterative construction: each number n is the set of its predecessors, and s(n) = n together with {n} is its successor.

The Dedekind induction principle: a statement holding of the empty set and passing from n to s(n) holds of every natural number; its defining unit is not among the imported sources, so the card injects it as a navigational label only.
Restriction of a function to a subset of its domain, and the image (range) and domain notations.
core_obligations: Prove by induction that no natural number is Dedekind infinite: the base case holds because the empty set admits no injection with proper-subset range.
Carry out the induction step by contraposition: suppose s(n) = n union {n} is Dedekind infinite via an injection f with range a proper subset of s(n); show n is Dedekind infinite.

Case n not in the range of f: restrict f to n; the restricted function g has range equal to the range of f minus the single value f(n), still a proper subset of the domain n, so n is Dedekind infinite.

Case n in the range of f: fix m in the domain of f but outside its range, and define h to agree with f except that the preimage of n is sent to m; injectivity of f then gives that n is not in the range of h, the range of h is a proper subset of s(n), and the Case 1 argument applied to h (after the same restriction) shows n is Dedekind infinite.
proof_roadmap: Contrapositive induction: the induction principle reduces the statement to showing s(n) Dedekind infinite implies n Dedekind infinite; the injection witnessing s(n) is repaired by either restriction (Case 1) or a one-point swap away from n (Case 2) into an injection witnessing n, and Case 2 reuses the Case 1 argument.
difficulty_reason: A contrapositive induction whose substantive step is the Case 2 swap construction: the reader must verify that sending the preimage of n to a fresh point m preserves injectivity and removes n from the range, and that the Case 1 restriction then applies verbatim.
